newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GM may supply engines to Russia's AvtoVAZ.
newsitem.headline: GM may supply engines to Russia's AvtoVAZ.

text.p: General Motors Corp said on Tuesday it was in advanced negotiations to supply engines to Russia's largest automaker AO AvtoVAZ, which makes Lada cars.

"Our talks certainly are in advanced stages," a GM spokesman told Reuters by telephone from his office in Zurich. "We hope to sign a contract in the not too distant future,... so we can start supplying engines this year."
GM's German automaker Adam Opel AG would supply AvtoVAZ with 2.0 litre ECOTEC engines from a plant in Kaiserslautern in southwest Germany, the official said.
AvtoVAZ would use the engines for a sportscar based on its new mid-sized sedan, code-named 2110, the spokesman said.
"Opel would supply the engines through a motorsport tuning facility in Britain that has developed rally cars for us," the spokesman said.
The number of the engines and the value of the contract remain undetermined, the spokesman said, adding, "It depends on the market."

GM, which already supplies AvtoVAZ with fuel-management systems, has been negotiating to form a joint venture with the Russian automaker and Finnish engineering group Valmet Oy. The venture would build cars, likely Opel Astras, in Russia at a new plant near Finland.
AvtoVAZ, increasingly plagued by problems with its cash flow and suppliers since the end of communism, has been trying to build cars with a major automaker to ensure its survival.
